chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

If the traveler does not find water, then let him seek it so long as he remains within the time. Then if he fears that the time will escape him, let him perform tayammum and pray at the end of the time. Then if he finds water, there is no makeup upon him, and let him perform wudu (ablution) for what he is to face afterward.

This report does not contradict the reports we cited in the chapter on repeating the prayer, which indicate that for one who prayed and then found water while time still remained, repetition is not obligatory upon him. For it may be said: if the obligation were connected to the end of the time, repetition would have been required of him; because we have already clarified the proper understanding of those reports, and we have said that the obligation is connected to the end of the time and no other understanding is permissible. We interpreted the statement, 'while time still remained,' to be connected to the state of the prayer, not to the existence of water; and on this basis there is no contradiction at all between these reports and those. As for what is contained in the report of 'Ali ibn Salim in the first chapter from the statement of the questioner, 'Should I perform tayammum and pray, then find water while some time still remains for me?' and he said, 'Do not repeat the prayer,' its intended sense is: 'Should I perform tayammum and pray while there remains for me enough time,' meaning the amount in which he may pray, so he prays and then the time exits.

key_terms.إِعَادَةِ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the prayer within its time
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water required for wudu (ablution) when available
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: the traveler who is the subject of the ruling
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the prescribed time of the prayer
key_terms.الْوُجُوبَ: the legal obligation discussed in relation to the end of prayer time
key_terms.فَلَا قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no makeup prayer required upon him
key_terms.فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ: let him perform tayammum as the substitute purification
key_terms.وَلْيَتَوَضَّأْ: let him perform wudu (ablution) afterward for future prayers

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler perform tayammum if water is unavailable, and must he repeat the prayer if he later finds water?
ai.summary: This report states that a traveler who cannot find water should continue seeking it during the prayer time, and only perform tayammum when fearing the expiration of the time. If he later finds water after praying with tayammum, he does not make up that prayer, but performs wudu (ablution) for subsequent prayers. The accompanying discussion explains how this ruling is reconciled with other reports by tying the obligation to the end of the prayer time.
